title: The Tally Card
passages:
Nour pressed the grease pencil to the board ledge. The metal was cold under her palm, and her fingers left black smudges on the steel. She drew the first run: Anza to Culvert Nine, six cases of cornmeal, receiving mark Br-4. She left a space and drew the second.

"Six cases cornmeal," Teodoro said, reading over her shoulder. "Br-4. That's Odessa Brill's mark. Culvert Nine pump station. She used to take our overflow before Anza went red."

Nour didn't answer. She drew the second line.

"Second run. Four cases of fuse wire. Br-4 again. You're sending wire to a dead pump station while the node's on half rations."

"Read and don't talk," Nour said.

"Third run. Two cases of canned milk. Br-4. Fourth run..." He stopped. Nour's hand had started to shake. She dragged the pencil across the ledger, scoring a thick wrong line before she could lift it.

"Fourth run," Teodoro said, quieter now. "Six cases of respirator scrubbers. Receiving mark Br-4. Canisters, Nour. The same ones caged under Rhea's brother's cot. Six cases of them riding in Odessa Brill's hoard at the end of the ore line while Ivo burns through his last cartridge in the shop."

Nour looked up. Her grease pencil snapped in two.

"Rhea's pumping him by hand," she said. "One cartridge left. Fenn put the relay shop on brown-out."

"Six cases of scrubbers means Ivo could run for weeks. Why didn't you tell me where the seals went before I had to pull Culvert Nine off a dead rig at post 71?"

"Because keeping my head down is wisdom," Nour said. "And because Brill burned once. Now she trusts a full storeroom over any person's promise. She doesn't hand anything over without a trade."

Teodoro wiped his hands on his rag. "So we don't trade her food. We trade her the scrubbers. Or we take them back."

"If we take them, Anza eats canisters and still starves. If we trade, she keeps the hoard and we get six cases of canisters and a promise from a woman who doesn't make promises."

"The scrubbers *are* the trade," Teodoro said. "Ivo needs them. The node needs the eleven seals cleaned. Culvert Nine is where the skim lives. You drew the map. Now you walk it."

Outside, the ore siding groaned. A ghost train cycled its couplers, a sound like bones in a tin can. Nour stared at the fourth line. Six cases. The same part number stamped on Ivo's cage. Brill had them, and Nour had put them there.

"When do we leave?" she asked.

"First light," Teodoro said. "If Fenn doesn't serve the warrant first."

Nour broke the second piece of pencil and drew a circle around Culvert Nine.
